topic: Complete history of Anita Porchet, Swiss watch enamellist
scope: Biography, training, career, clients, techniques, awards, teaching and studio history of Anita Porchet, as documented in publicly accessible sources. Cutoff: 2026-11-26.
coverage_status: unverified: no independent second researcher, so no capture-recapture bound could be computed

claims.claim: Born 15 January 1961 in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland
Learned enamelling from her godfather, a watch engraver; grew up around his workshop
Attended the Ecole d'Arts Appliques in La Chaux-de-Fonds for a preparatory year, then the Lausanne art school from 1980
Earned the federal engraving and enamelling certificate in 1984 (Haute Ecole Arc)
Completed a further artistic aptitude certificate at the Lausanne cantonal art school in 1985
Learned from enamellists Elisabeth Juillerat and Suzanne Rohr; Wikipedia calls Rohr her apprenticeship master
Taught crafts and enamelling at the School of Applied Arts in La Chaux-de-Fonds from 1985 to 1992
claims.verified_by: europastar ('six years teaching' in La Chaux-de-Fonds before going freelance); theweek ('taught in a school for six years')
claims.status: confirmed (duration corroborated; exact years from one source)

claims.claim: Teaching began in 2008
claims.verified_by: contradicted by c7 sources; Homo Faber page is also internally inconsistent ('taught for the past ten years')
claims.status: disputed - likely refers to later workshop teaching, not school teaching

claims.claim: Started her career in 1988
claims.verified_by: none; conflicts in spirit with c7 teaching start and c10 studio dates

claims.claim: Opened her own studio in Lausanne in 1993
claims.verified_by: wikipedia (1993 Lausanne studio); europastar (studio set up early 1990s)

claims.claim: Homo Faber gives 1994 for the workshop opening
claims.status: disputed - 1993 vs 1994 across sources; 1993 is better corroborated

claims.claim: Moved the studio to Corcelles-le-Jorat (Route de la Goille); had worked there for about 17 years as of 2016 to 2018 reporting
claims.status: confirmed for current location; move date approximately 2009 by inference

claims.claim: Very first watches she enamelled date to the mid-1990s; first dials made at Patek Philippe's request
Works for Patek Philippe since the early 1990s / 1995
Clients include Patek Philippe, Vacheron Constantin, Piaget, Chanel, Hermes, Chaumet, Audemars Piguet, Jaquet Droz, Fabergé
claims.verified_by: watchonista; robb report; wikipedia; no official brand page confirmed
claims.status: confirmed by multiple media sources; brand primary sources not accessible

claims.claim: Techniques: cloisonne, champleve, paillonne, grisaille, miniature painting, plique-a-jour, Limoges
Dial enamel is crushed by hand in an agate mortar and fired at around 800 C for 30 to 90 seconds per firing
A complex dial can take up to a year to finish; studio employs three apprentices
claims.status: confirmed for apprentices; year-long timeline single-source

claims.claim: Dawn on the Lake pocket watch made for Patek Philippe's 175th anniversary; miniature Palais Garnier ceiling for Vacheron Constantin
claims.verified_by: watchonista (Palais Garnier, Dawn on the Lake)

claims.claim: Won the 2015 Prix Gaia in the artisan-creation category, the first woman to do so
claims.verified_by: watchonista (Nov 20 2015); quill and pad ('a woman has finally won'); first-woman wording is inferred from 21 years of male winners, not stated outright

claims.claim: Shared the 2017 Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Geneve Special Jury Prize with Suzanne Rohr
Received the Fondation de la Haute Horlogerie Hommage au Talent award and a Vaud cultural heritage prize
Her work uses paillons from stock dating to the early nineteenth century
Widely described as the best-known enamel artist working in watches

positions: 1985-1992 at La Chaux-de-Fonds school (watchonista, wikipedia; corroborated by europastar six years and theweek six years)
disputes.resolution: Best supported: school teaching 1985-1992. The 2008 date likely refers to a later teaching role in her own workshop. Unresolved; the Homo Faber page is internally inconsistent.
1993 preferred (two sources, one of them the more detailed); 1994 may refer to a different milestone.

positions: Certificate in 1984 (confirmed by europastar and watchonista)
disputes.resolution: Certificate 1984 confirmed. The 1984 Patek Philippe prize is single-source and unverified.
Clients confirmed by multiple sources; exact start years not established.
